To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

patients in Egypt evaluate healthcare service quality based on eight constructs: hospital premises and hospital employees, doctor's medical services, nursing medical services, diagnostic medical services, admission, discharge, rooms and housekeeping, and meals.

the constructs and sub-constructs of HSQ that have a significant effect on patients' perception of service quality in Egypt are: hospital premises and employee tangibles; physician reliability; physician interaction; nursing tangibles, nursing interaction; admission knowledge and courteousness; meals tangibles, rooms tangibles and courteousness, and discharge courteousness and knowledge.

the eight constructs and 17 sub constructs of HSQ in Egypt are: hospital premises and staff; doctor; nursing; diagnostic medical service (including diagnostic medical service reliability); admission (including admission responsiveness); discharge (including discharge knowledge and courtesy); rooms and housekeeping (including rooms and housekeeping tangibles); and meals (including meals tangibles).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the constructs and sub-constructs of HSQ, the effect of each of the sub-constructs on the patients' overall perception, and the impact of the sub- constructs on each other.

the development of a model that encompasses all constructs and sub-constructs consumers use in evaluating HSQ in Egypt, and to identify the sub-constructs and examine the effect that each of them has on patients' overall HSQ.

(2) how are the sub-constructs related to the overall perception of healthcare service quality? and (3) what are the implications of the results for healthcare service providers?
